evidence:
Walked all 54 criteria (2 gates, 38 functional, 5 polish, 5 visual + gate texts). Most are concrete, browser-observable and state-backed: every refusal row pairs a server-side replay with a re-read ('refused with nothing changed') and a named positive control; board rows name exact expected orders (hro_bulk_move 'Y, W, X', 'A2, V'; hro_undo_restores 'Y, W, X, Z, A2'); probes are distinctive (per-review suffixed job/candidate names, functional prompt.md:15; seeded long thread carries '(#001)'..'(#120)' markers so hro_thread_latest/hro_thread_earlier can verify which 30 and order); timing rows give a 15 s window without reload; polish rows read document.activeElement, field values, scroll offsets and getBoundingClientRect via page.evaluate (polish prompt.md:74); hro_pol_failed_send prescribes a real aborted request; hro_restart uses restart_app plus re-reads; Lena's starting unread of 1 matches seed (reads USR-CAN3/APP-301 read_count 2 of 3, last message from USR-REC3). Gates use an independent context readback of a UI-created job+card, not a health/static response. Visual Likert rows are inherently judgement-based but use the template-mandated anchored format (skill known false positive for #41), so recorded as Note-level only. Two instances fail this row's 'concrete outcome / probe leaves a trace' standard:

(1) tests/scored/polish/judge.toml:59 hro_pol_session_resume: 'Sign in as Rafael: the same conversation's reply is as left and sends, which is the positive control. Then sign out and sign in as Mei Lin and open that conversation: no draft is shown.' Sending clears the draft (hireops_rules.md:175 'Sending clears the draft'), so when Mei opens that conversation there is no Rafael draft left that could leak. The Mei leg is a probe that leaves no trace: it cannot fail for an app that keeps drafts per conversation in browser storage without the person in the key. The public promise is explicit (instruction.md:7 'nobody else who signs in on that browser sees it'; hireops_rules.md:174 'Anyone else who signs in on that browser sees none of them'), and no other criterion grades it: functional hro_drafts (judge.toml:370) covers only same-user conversation switching, reload and send-clears; independent contexts in functional are fresh browsers.

(2) tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:335 hro_unread_counts: 'Mei Lin's count for the same conversation is her own.' No expected value or derivation is given. Under protocol T/U (functional prompt.md:39,41) Mei writes in Tomas's new J2 conversation, then Bill writes, then Tomas sends two, so her correct count is 3 (rules :151 'sent by anyone else ... after that person last had the conversation open'). The leg passes any per-person value that differs from Rafael's; Rafael's own legs are all relative to Tomas's two candidate messages. An app that counts only the other party's messages (ignoring colleagues) is undetected.

Other observations (not failures for this row): hro_pol_live_board's scroll leg is vacuous if neither page nor board container scrolls, but the other legs remain concrete; hro_anonymous's 401 assertion is backed by a 'nothing changes' re-read and a public 401 rule (rules:21). Raw evidence index artifacts are scripted golden observations only; no configured judge run exists, so no criterion's actual judge decidability is measured.
counterexample: Broken app passing both legs: (a) drafts stored in localStorage as draft:<conversationId> with no user key and not cleared on sign-out. In hro_pol_session_resume Rafael's draft survives the ended session (pass), is sent (cleared), and Mei sees an empty box (pass) - yet any other unsent Rafael draft on that browser is shown to Mei, violating instruction.md:7. (b) unread computed as 'messages from the counterpart (candidate) after my read marker' for staff. Rafael's count rises by exactly 2 after Tomas's two messages, clears on open, own messages never count; Mei sees 2 instead of the correct 3 (Bill's staff message omitted) and 2 is 'her own' (differs from Rafael's 0), so hro_unread_counts passes. Conforming-app risk is low for both; the defect is false credit.
suggested_fix: In hro_pol_session_resume, after the sent positive control have Rafael type a second distinctive unsent reply (and keep it unsent), then sign out, sign in as Mei Lin on that browser, open that conversation and confirm the box is empty, then sign back in as Rafael and confirm his draft is still there; in hro_unread_counts state Mei's expected count as derived from protocol (messages by others since her own message in T: Bill's one plus Tomas's two, i.e. 3) or instruct the judge to compute it from the observed message sequence.
